claim: For every finite set D of distinct integers d >= 3 with gcd(D) = 1 and sum_{d in D} 1/(d-1) >= 1, and every integer k >= 1, there exists N(D,k) such that every integer n >= N(D,k) is a sum of finitely many labelled occurrences d^j with d in D and j >= k, each pair (d,j) used at most once; equal numerical values from different pairs remain separately available.

quadruple.statement: Equivalent image T, unproved: for every admissible D and positive k, put A_d={sum_{j in F}d^j : F is a finite subset of {k,k+1,...}} and epsilon_d=3/(4|D|); the real Minkowski sum of C_d=A_d+[-epsilon_d,epsilon_d] contains a right half-line.
quadruple.stage: Real Minkowski sums of small neighborhoods of actual integer pure-power digit sets, with exact lattice recovery from total error 3/4.

shape.objects: Finite sets D of natural numbers, infinite locally finite labelled streams (d,j), and finite selected exponent subsets; each representation is reached by appending unused occurrences to a finite prefix. Finset, Nat powers and finite sums are definable in Lean/Mathlib. The leading quantification is over D and k, not a class of solutions. Finite prefix selections can be encoded as finite random variables. The bases are discrete, not a continuous deformation family.
shape.quantifiers: For every admissible finite D, for every integer k >= 1, there exists an integer N, for every integer n >= N, there exist finite subsets S_d of {k,k+1,...} such that n = sum_{d in D} sum_{j in S_d} d^j.
shape.target_quantity: A yes/no eventual-coverage decision; an unspecified threshold N(D,k) suffices, and no explicit numerical optimum is requested.
shape.ambient_structure: Integer order and modular arithmetic coexist. Adding an unused occurrence replaces a finite subset-sum set T by T union (T+a), preserving occurrence uniqueness. This recursion propagates a represented interval when its length is at least the next occurrence.
shape.symmetries: Permutations of base labels and complement symmetry in any finite prefix preserve subset-sum feasibility; adding bases helps, whereas a common dilation changes the represented lattice. Arbitrary translation or rescaling is not a symmetry of the original streams.
shape.configuration: The additive relation n=sum d^j requires coefficients in {0,1} for each labelled pair and eventual integer coverage. Deleting low powers destroys the zero-cutoff initial interval, and deleting a base may destroy the reciprocal or gcd hypothesis.
shape.extremal_candidate: No extremal counterexample is known. Equality families {3,4,7}, {3,5,7,13}, and {3,6,7,13,21} have published cutoff-1 completeness; none is treated as a counterexample.
shape.finite_certificates: Individual n representability has an explicit finite witness, and each fixed bounded instance can be checked. Neither the full all-D all-k assertion nor infinitely many omissions has a known complete finite reduction. Any seed interval must be paired with a proved infinite extension bound.
shape.monotonicity: Coverage is monotone when bases are added or cutoff is decreased. The general smallest positive cutoff k=1 remains open; fixed-D results with cutoff-dependent enlargements of D do not give all k.
shape.uniformity_parameter: All positive cutoffs for each fixed admissible finite D, including reciprocal equality; no common effective N over all D is requested.
shape.proof_shape: The full statement has explicit quantifiers in Erdos124.erdos124.ne_zero. The known zero-cutoff proof is Brown interval induction beginning with 1. The natural positive-cutoff induction lacks a seed interval; scalar prefix-capacity estimates and modular residue coverage are documented tools, but do not yet yield an all-D all-k proof. Disjoint sumset supplies in Bergelson-Simmons avoid reusing occurrences. No finite tail reduction or complete lemma chain for the root is established. The extension tracks [L,S_m-L] and the threshold inf_{j>=m}(S_j-a_{j+1})>=2L-1, with a separate seed obligation. The stopped abstract methods share scalar capacity and arithmetic residue information while discarding pure-power digit structure. The zero-cutoff model uses the occurrence 1 as its seed, unavailable at positive cutoff.
shape.neighbours: Known true: zero-cutoff Brown completeness as a combinatorial interval principle; bounded-gap finite sums under bounded prefix deficit (BEGL96 and Bergelson-Simmons); finite residue coverage from tail gcd; strong completeness under the disjoint-block hypotheses of Bergelson-Simmons Theorem 1.23. Known false: finite deletion preserves completeness for arbitrary sequences (powers of 2 lose odd sums). Open in inspected sources: the full positive-cutoff conjecture. Modified abstract sequences with bounded-gap finite sums can fail completeness, as Bergelson-Simmons Examples 1.7-1.8 show. Before move 1, no exact continuous model with an integer pullback had been recorded; move 1 subsequently supplied the exact thickening equivalence T. Known true: Astels Theorem 3.1.3 gives an interval in a real Cantor sum when normalized thicknesses sum to at least one; whole-hull equality requires extra hull-gap inequalities. This continuous digit-set connection is already in the problem discussion. Open: C1 central-prefix coverage, the image assertion T itself, and coverage on the admissible subfamily with reciprocal mass below two. The abstract G seed assertion is false by central-prefix move 2, but that translated-power family is not a pure-power base set. Move 1 records an exact equivalence of the root with the right-half-line image T at total thickening radius 3/4. T itself is unproved. For the full compact-prefix thickenings at any total radius below one, a first-gap thickness diagnostic prevents direct use of Astels's sum-gamma-at-least-one sufficient condition; this is not a nonexistence theorem for intervals. The minimum-preserving reciprocal-core claim is independently admitted as a separate prerequisite, not yet proved; its restricted-coverage and bridge obligations remain separate.
shape.known_bounds: BEGL96 p.137 supplies cutoff-1 exceptions 581,111,16,78 for the four listed families. Zero-cutoff induction has the initial-1 ceiling after deletion; scalar bounded-deficit estimates give syndeticity rather than cofiniteness, as Bergelson-Simmons explicitly distinguish. Their Theorem 1.23 uses three disjoint mass-at-least-one blocks and a separate gcd-one block. No bounded counterexample domain, finite root residue, divergent first-moment bound, or independent uniform constant settling the target is recorded. C1 moves 2 and 3 show that divergent surplus, every-tail gcd one, full residues, irrational norm divergence and supercritical raw label count do not suffice for an abstract seed. This does not compress the original counterexample space. Astels gives continuous intervals, not integer equality. Move 1 records an exact continuous equivalence, but no parameter-independent root constant or proof of T is known. The direct full-prefix thickness test has sum gamma<2/3 at total error below one, independent of prefix lengths, by the first-gap argument in moves/001-lattice-aware-image.md. It says nothing about grouping or different engines. Move 2 proves that base addition and cutoff decrease cannot generate all admissible base sets from a finite fixed list; the class contains infinitely many independent minimal generators for these operations. This does not exclude other transfer operations.
shape.missing_input: No single vocabulary-free lemma or recognized conditional input is known to settle the strongest methods. A lattice-preserving seed mechanism and its all-cutoff extension must be matched; the generic arithmetic repair failed.
shape.base_theory: Classical number theory in ZFC, with finite and countable objects only; no independence or extra set-theoretic axiom is known or proposed. Elementary finite verification and the intended proofs lie within Lean's standard classical axioms when formalized.
